results.title: Differential Detection - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
results.content: Differential Detection is a method used in digital modulation schemes like PSK, where the phase shifts between symbols are detected based on the phase differences rather than the absolute phase values. In all cases, the information is encoded within the intensity of the light, but with RZ and CRZ modulation, “1s” are encoded by pulses as depicted in Figure 5.10. In order to detect the optical signal and to convert it back to a digital electrical signal, light is sent onto a photodiode, which is followed by a low pass filter (with a 3 dB bandwidth around 0.7×bitrate) so as to integrate the signal over a bit duration. In order to maximize performance of undersea systems, and before the adoption of coherent detection, phase shift keying (PSK) and differential detection at the receiver side were introduced commercially around 2007 under the name of differential phase shift keying (DPSK) or differential binary phase shift keying (DBPSK), with B indicating that a binary modulation is used.
